items.title: Branford Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: I saw you at that concert you played with Sonny, man.

ctx.x: Are there other people like Trane, or even approximate that level?

Coleman Hawkins had that kind of…. Younger musicians had that kind of reverence for him. Sonny Rollins is, to this day, still in awe of Coleman Hawkins. Coleman had that thing…. There’s a great recording of Coleman Hawkins toward the end of his life doing this record. It’s not a very good record. It’s a combination of strings and big band. It’s called “The Hawk Flies High in the Land of Hi-Fi.” They were doing these hi-fi records. MRC was doing these records and that was the thing. Cannonball Adderley in hi-fi,…

know, here is the guy who was playing in the twenties, when Charlie Parker, learning how to play like him, and then he’s - I don’t know how old he was, he was probably in his sixties – he’s playing like Bird. Like, just to humble yourself to that degree, to go from being the master to the student, is some of the most inspiring stuff that I have ever heard. And I can understand why Sonny revered him so much. Cause Hawk was always trying to get to the next thing. When the big bands died away, and the small groups…
